questions.question: A team evaluates an LLM before production rollout. Which evaluation practices are sound? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Reporting only the single best run as the final metric
Judging quality from a single cherry-picked example
Checking for bias across demographic groups
Measuring accuracy on a representative test set

questions.explanation: Reliable LLM evaluation should use representative datasets and assess fairness across different groups. Relying on a single best run or a cherry-picked example can produce misleading conclusions and does not reflect real-world performance.

questions.question: A developer wants to build a question-answering app over private PDFs using LangChain. Which components are typically used? (Select all that apply)

options.text: A module that renders the PDFs as printed pages
Document loaders to ingest the PDFs
A vector store to hold embeddings for retrieval
Embedding each PDF page as a single fixed 3-dimensional vector

questions.explanation: A typical LangChain RAG pipeline uses document loaders to ingest PDF content, embedding models to create vector representations, and a vector store for semantic retrieval. Modern embeddings usually contain hundreds or thousands of dimensions, not a fixed 3-dimensional vector.

questions.question: An agent occasionally loops indefinitely without finishing a task. Which controls help? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Setting a maximum number of steps or iterations
Imposing a time or token budget per task
Adding a termination check when the goal is met
Removing all stopping conditions so it keeps trying

questions.explanation: Agent systems commonly use guardrails such as maximum iteration limits, time or token budgets, and goal-completion checks to prevent infinite loops. Removing stopping conditions increases the risk of endless execution.
